data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit root 'lahara', meaning 'to flow' or 'wave'. In Hindu mythology, Lahar is a name of Lord Vishnu, representing the continuous flow of life. It is also the name of the goddess of fertility and motherhood. The name Lahar carries the meaning “Wave, Flow” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lahar usually hope their child will grow to embody wave, flow and live with faith, good character and purpose.

This name can also be associated with the various waves in Hindu mythology, such as the waves in the ocean or the waves of time, symbolizing the continuous flow and transformation of life.

It is a name that encourages us to cherish and appreciate the present moment while understanding that change is inevitable. Additionally, the name Lahar is associated with Lord Vishnu, who is the preserver of life and the embodiment of love and compassion. In essence, the name Lahar serves as a reminder of the importance of embracing change and savoring the flow of life, spiritual and otherwise.

historical_references.reference: Lahar was also a king of the Haihai tribe in ancient India, mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas. He is known for his valor and is considered to be a hero of the Haihai.
